newsitem.title: UK: Ibstock shares drop after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Ibstock shares drop after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Ibstock Plc dropped on Wednesday after the building materials and forest products group warned of lower full-year profits as first-half results were hit by low paper pulp prices and a weak housing market.
Ibstock shares dropped to a year low of 56p in early trade but recovered marginally to trade at 57p by 0716 GMT, down 7-1/2p on the day. The overall market was stable.
Ibstock said it expected pre-tax profits for 1996 would be "significantly less than for 1995." It said it did not expect half-year losses at its pulp division to be recovered by the end of the year.
Ibstock earnings dropped to 2.4 million stg in the first half from 14 million a year earlier.
Analysts said the results were well below expectations and would prompt hefty cuts in earnings forecasts.

"Obviously, we weren't looking for figures quite this bad...We had been looking for full-year profits of 19 million stg against 26 million previously and that now looks unattainable," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The analyst said that despite consolidation in the crucial brick market, "predatory pricing" remained the norm, and the pulp division gave cause for concern.

Ibstock said earlier on Wednesday that it was seeking to reduce costs and improve margins in the brick sector. Its share of that UK market is expected to total around 30 percent after it combines its operations with rival Redland Plc.
